post.title: 15-year vs 30-year mortgage: $337,000 less interest
post.ig:
$798 more a month saves $337K in interest.
Example: a $400,000 loan at Freddie Mac's Sept 24, 2026 averages (30-year 7.03%, 15-year 6.42%). Rates change weekly.
30-year: $2,669 a month, $560,939 total interest.
15-year: $3,467 a month, $224,035 total interest, paid off 15 years sooner.
The trade-off: the 30-year's lower payment frees up monthly cash.
Sources: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey; standard amortization math (principal and interest only).
